results.title: Attacked by official tour guide
results.text:
I was racially attacked by a registered tour guide at the ticket booth for saying that the 1000R entry fee for tourists was a bit crazy. I was verbally assault by this man and mocked, he stated “oh look at the white foreigner can’t pay 10 dollars in” and he then stated “ your kind came here and murdered our ancestors. 

Things escalated so quickly with this man other tour guides and eventually the tourist police had to become involved. I was in fear of my safety.   This man attacked me in front of many people and publicly humiliated me.  He also after I called him out as a racist accused me of being racist. 

This man an employee of the Guide Association of Pashupatinath, is meeting tourists from around the world in a places of worship, filled with that kind of hate and racism. I have never in my life been treated with such a total lack of respect or dignity. It was plain to see from this man’s behavior that tourists are not welcome here. I would advise you to avoid it at all cost. It’s not worth the hassle or the entry fee. What a waste of a day, 

UNSAFE FOR TOURISTS

AVOID AVOID AVOID

results.title: Pashupatinath at Dusk
results.text: My visit to Pashupatinath in the evening was an experience I will not soon forget. The sight, sounds and the scent in the air brought together a time I have little to compare to.  We watched and listened from the hillside in the forest with a birds eye view as the daylight fell and darkness, music, prayers and sweet smoke filled the evening sky.

results.title: One of the 8 UNESCO Cultural Heritage Site Must visit for all No mater of Hindu or Not
results.text:
Pashupatinath Temple is one of the 8 UNESCO Cultural Heritage Sites of the Kathmandu Valley

Dedicated to Lord Shiva, Pashupatinath is one of the four most important religious sites in Asia for devotees of Shiva. Built in the 5th century and later renovated by Malla kings, the site itself is said to have existed from the beginning of the millennium when a Shiva lingam was discovered here.

The largest temple complex in Nepal, it stretches on both sides of the Bagmati River which is considered holy by Hindus. The main pagoda style temple has a gilded roof, four sides covered in silver, and wood carvings of the finest quality. Temples dedicated to several other Hindu and Buddhist deities surround the temple of Pashupatinath.

Just outside the temple complex you will find 100s of little shops selling Pooja Offerings and selling traditional Nepali Gurkha Hats and One can also buy locally harvested Rudarkash Beens too

results.title: Go with a good Hindi guide!
results.text:
This is not a place to visit without a devout Hindi guide who can explain the rites of preparation of the body for cremation so that you can understand the process and what is happening in front of you.  This is a place to put away your camera and respectfully watch and listen - remember the people  around you are mourning the loss of a loved one.  This is not a place for children.

This experience may change how you think about death.

results.title: Thought provoking
results.text:
Pashupati is a spiritual place where people come to die with their feet in the water. They are moved from the dying rooms to the water’s edge in their final moments. We watched as the recently deceased were bathed by their families and wrapped in cloth and flower garlands. and sprinkled with a red powder.  After a short ceremony they were moved to the burning ghats. Here the funeral pyre is lit and the body burned.

It sounds quite macabre and a bit voyeuristic but it was actually very touching to watch families take care of their loved ones and prepare them for their final journey. It is a place of quiet contemplation but will the usual Asian hustle and bustle (such as someone selling candy floss!)

It costs 1000 NPR to enter the site and it’s worth going if you haven’t been to a site like this before.

results.title: A must visit when in Kathmandu
results.text:
Pashupatinath Temple complex is Nepal’s holiest Hindu Shrine, it’s situated along the banks of river Bagmati. Before the temple complex one can witness cremations as it’s where the devot send their dead to the next world.
The complex is really huge & if one is a tourist the one must hv a guide to assist on what’s happening as you enter the compounds thru the golden gate.. in a complex of statues & deities one has to pass by & with a guide one understands what each is related to in Hindu religion... quite a bit of walking inside is covered by bare foot hence be prepared... some loose Rupee notes or coins are needed if one wants to offer to the deities.
